title: Migrating a pywraplp model to MathOpt

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A pywraplp line s = solver.NumVar(0, solver.infinity(), "spare") is ported as s = model.add_variable(name="spare"). The model minimizes 9s + 4q with the row s + q >= 10 and 0 <= q <= 30. What can the port return for s?

options.text: 0, the old answer, since MathOpt variables are nonnegative unless told otherwise
options.says: MathOpt's add_variable left out bounds at -inf and inf in the lesson's run.

options.text: Nothing, since MathOpt refuses a variable created with no bounds given
options.says: The lesson created variables with no bounds and printed their bounds as -inf and inf.

options.text: A negative value, since a bound left out of add_variable is infinite
options.says: Right: without lb=0 the variable may go below 0; port NumVar(0, ...) as add_variable(lb=0).

options.text: A whole number, since add_variable makes integers unless told otherwise
options.says: add_variable makes a continuous variable; add_integer_variable makes an integer one.

origin.section: Every pywraplp Call Has a MathOpt Counterpart

questions.stem: An analyst wants to try one MathOpt selection model on HiGHS, SCIP and CP-SAT and compare the values. How does the code do it?

options.text: Build the model once, then call solve with each SolverType in turn
options.says: Right: the lesson built the model once and solved it with HIGHS, GSCIP and CP_SAT.

options.text: Build the model three times, once inside each solver's own object
options.says: That is how pywraplp works; a MathOpt model does not belong to a solver.

options.text: Build the model once, then convert it to CP-SAT's own format for that run
options.says: The same model was passed to CP_SAT unchanged and returned the same value.

options.text: Build the model once, then export it as LP text for the other two runs
options.says: No export is needed; solve takes the model and a SolverType.

origin.section: MathOpt Keeps the Model Apart From the Solver

questions.stem: A port test on a large instance fails: the pywraplp script reports OPTIMAL at 512,400 and the MathOpt port OPTIMAL at 512,430, with default parameters in both. Each plan keeps the other model's rules. What is the next step?

options.text: Mark the port as wrong, since two optimal values of one model are equal
options.says: OPTIMAL means within the gap tolerance; the lesson's medium run gave two optimal values $5k apart.

options.text: Compare the two plans, since equal plans would prove equal models
options.says: Optimal plans can differ when several tie; the lesson compares values and checks plans against rules.

options.text: Raise the old script's time limit, since its search stopped too early
options.says: A run stopped by a limit reports FEASIBLE; both reported OPTIMAL within their gaps.

options.text: Set the gap to 0 in both and compare again, since each optimal value has a tolerance
options.says: Right: pywraplp's default gap is 0.0001; at gap 0 the lesson's medium values agreed.

origin.section: A Port Is Proved by a Test: Same Value at Zero Gap, and Each Plan Allowed by the Other's Rules
